title: EFFICACY OF PROPRANOLOL IN TRAUMATIC BRAIN INJURY PATIENTS ADMITTED TO THE ICU: A PROSPECTIVE, RANDOMIZED, TRIPLE-BLIND STUDY (ProP TBI in ICU)
official: EFFICACY OF PROPRANOLOL IN TRAUMATIC BRAIN INJURY PATIENTS ADMITTED TO THE ICU: A PROSPECTIVE, RANDOMIZED, TRIPLE-BLIND STUDY (ProP TBI in ICU)
summary: Main objective: To compare in-hospital mortality in patients with TBI requiring ICU admission after receiving 14 days of treatment with propranolol versus placebo
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Patients aged 18 or under 80 years (both inclusive) who have suffered a moderate or severe TBI (GCS 3-13) and require ICU admission
2. Informed consent must be signed by the patient or their legal representative if the patient is unable to do so
3. Before starting the trial, the patient must be hemodynamically stable, defined as having a systolic blood pressure (SBP) greater than 110 mmHg, cerebral perfusion pressure (CPP) greater than 60 mmHg (in patients with ICP monitoring), and a heart rate (HR) greater than 60 beats per minute. Patients with these hemodynamic parameters may be included with a dose lower than 0.10 mcg/kg/min of norepinephrine base
4. Study start within the first 96 hours after the injury
Exclusion criteria:
1. Age 17 years or younger or 81 years or older (both included)
2. Preexisting asthma or bronchospasm
3. Patients with spinal cord injuries
4. Patients with bilateral mydriasis upon admission
5. Patients with a poor prognosis and a life expectancy of less than 24 hours
6. Pregnant women
7. Patients for whom follow-up at 1 month and 6 months cannot be guaranteed
8. Patients unable to take oral medication due to swallowing problems and for whom nasogastric tube placement is not indicated
9. Patients enrolled in another clinical trial
10. Hemodynamically unstable patients, defined as systolic blood pressure less than 109 mmHg, cerebral perfusion pressure less than 59 mmHg (in patients with ICP monitoring), and heart rate less than 59 beats per minute, who require norepinephrine base at doses greater than 0.11 mcg/kg/min
11. Lactic acid greater than 2 mmol/L at the time of randomization
12. Patients with a history of TBI for more than 96 hours
13. Polytrauma patients with an extracranial Injury Severity Score greater than 18 points or an extracranial AIS score ≥4 points in any region
14. Patients with penetrating TBI
15. Preexisting heart disease that contraindicates beta-blockers, such as first-, second-, or third-degree heart block without a permanent pacemaker; heart failure defined as an ejection fraction less than 40%
16. Patients on home treatment with digoxin, diltiazem, or verapamil
17. Patients on beta-blocker treatment prior to admission
